title: Aeroradiometric map and geologic interpretation of part of the Cape Fear region, Florence and Georgetown 1 degree x 2 degrees quadrangles, South Carolina
citation: Owens, J.P., Grosz, A.E., and Fisher, J.C., 1989, Aeroradiometric map and geologic interpretation of part of the Cape Fear region, Florence and Georgetown 1 degree x 2 degrees quadrangles, South Carolina: U.S. Geological Survey Miscellaneous Investigations Series Map I-1948-B, map scale 1:250,000.
notes: Single OCR sheet whose columns are interleaved line by line; quotes are fragments of one line. Units from the Regional Geology section (South Carolina part of the Florence and Georgetown quadrangles). Tables 1-6 (gamma-ray spectra, mineralogy, neutron activation, monazite/zircon) are too garbled in the OCR to read reliably and were not recorded; they are radiometric and mineral analyses, not water or rock tests. Aeroradiometric contours (total-count, 25 counts per second interval) are geophysical, not a geologic surface. Age conflicts: Penholoway 'middle Pleistocene' in the text vs 'lower Pleistocene' in the explanation; argillite 'Lower Cambrian' in the text vs 'Middle Cambrian' in the explanation.
